points: Yields have risen sharply since summer, driven by weakening economic conditions combined with persistent inflation and higher Fed borrowing costs — not debt concerns.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: The deeper reason behind surging bond yields

headlines: Bond yields are surging due to economic weakness combined with persistent inflation and higher Federal Reserve borrowing costs, not debt concerns.
Paychex reported a 'low-hire, low-fire' environment, signaling employers are cautious about expansion despite labor market tightness.
Wage and commodity inflation are squeezing corporate margins: General Mills warned of sustained pressure from wheat, diesel, and packaging costs.
Restaurant traffic is collapsing as gas prices consume household disposable income: Cracker Barrel down 6.1%, Olive Garden up just 1.1%.

sections.title: The Economic Weakness Behind Rising Yields
points: Bond yields have risen sharply starting in summer, driven by weakening economic conditions under the tightening grip of inflation.
The Federal Reserve's higher interest rates make borrowing costlier for both businesses and consumers, amplifying economic strain.
BlackRock's chief investment officer Rick Rieder called the situation 'not a crisis but an eye-opener,' requiring careful consideration by investors.

sections.title: Corporate Red Flags Showing Economic Slowdown
points: Paychex executives reported a 'low-hire, low-fire' environment, indicating businesses are hesitant to expand hiring or make workforce cuts—a cautious posture.
General Mills warned of multiple quarters of pressured profit margins due to surging inflation in wheat, diesel, and packaging materials.
Cracker Barrel traffic dropped 6.1% in the most recent quarter; Olive Garden sales grew only 1.1%, both pointing to consumer spending constraints.
Higher gas prices are eroding household disposable income, forcing consumers to cut back on discretionary spending like dining out.
